items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: So Clifford Jordan was as important as anything that ever we came with in Strata-East because it helped to further jumpstart this venture.

ctx.x: Okay. Okay. It didn’t emerge from the Civil Rights Movement because my idea to do an independent endeavor like this stemmed from let’s say two events. First of all, when I was coming up and you really got into this, you either got your own leader date at Blue Note or one of the other independents that was going on at the time. That didn’t happen to me nor did it happen for Woody Shaw, because both of us were coming up at the same time. It should have, you know, because of who we recorded with on Blue Note. Both…

completely different in terms of the historical thing of my career had that happened. So by 1968, ’69, I was already, I already had this what was going to become Strata-East records. I was going to do it, it was just a matter of time. And because my dear Stanley Cowell and I were so close you know, every day, and working with Max Roach and watching what he did it was inevitable at that particular time, in 1970, that we were going to go in the studio and make a recording which would be the first record to launch…
Can I pause for a moment there. Are you saying that the artists had their recordings already completed and they came to you for whatever your label could offer?
